diagram_math_checks.result: All four vertices are M_{n×1}(F); A, B and invertible P are n×n matrices acting on the left. Top-row columns are C-coordinates and bottom-row columns are B-coordinates. These are the column-space objects explicitly used in proof step 3.1, and are valid also for n=0.

The local def-change-of-basis-matrix defines P_{Y←X} as conversion from X to Y coordinates. Thus proof step 2.1 uses P=P_{B←C}, giving c_B=P c_C, so both vertical arrows must point down from the C row to the B row.

The Statement identifies A=[T]_B^B and B=[T]_C^C. Therefore the top map is left multiplication by B and the bottom map by A. Down then right is AP, right then down is PB; AP=PB is equivalent to the exact B=P^{-1}AP relation from step 2.1. The two-sided formula supplier agrees with this order.
The actual native image has four column-space nodes, two rightward horizontal arrows labelled B and A, and two downward arrows labelled P; all labels and edges appear without clipping or overlap.
